newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up on foreign buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on Thursday after two days of profit-taking, as investors got back into stocks of firms expected to do have done well in results up to June, brokers said.

The all share index closed 4.0 points up at 820.7. Blue chips Development Development Finance rose four rupees to 310, Colombo Dockyard one to 25.50, Hatton National Bank five to 285, Sampath Bank two to 79.

"Buyers stayed on the sidelines in the first hours of trading to see if their absence would continue to bring prices down," said Alistair Corera of brokerge Forbes & Walker. "The index rose in the last hour after after investors saw prices remain firm."
Turnover was 94.2 million rupees, mainly due to foreign buying of blue chips Asian Hotels and Sampath Bank. A foreign investors also bought 75,000 Tea Services.

"Corporate results to June which are due later this month are expected to be good. Therefore, investors are getting into stocks which are expected to do well," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena of Ceylinco Stock Brokers.
